title: Reverb and effect algorithms and the factory programs — program data
notes: Values of coefficient words are exact (word / 2^23). Delays of the effect lines in samples for the extended delay memory (r = 32); keys ending in _std for the standard memory (r = 2), document 11.1.
Patches from sources other than ADJUST are evaluated at source value 0 ("patch at rest").
AP Sweep pairs at rest gain with stock signs; Concert Hall / Glide>Hall modulated taps are a snapshot.
Res1 programs show the unassigned resonator state (tuning word 6011780, feedback 0), document 13.4.
tempo_bpm is the 16-bit program tempo (section 16.3); four programs are stored above 250 BPM.

A stored value with "locked": true is the code 32*den + num = num/den beats (16.3). A patch with "tempo_coded": true has points 32*num + den (points_beats gives num/den, 16.6); a parameter set by such a patch carries effective_beats.
Every parameter runs from 0 to its "max" (stored pages, Mod page and parameters in effect; 14.6). The effect voice delays are further limited by the delay memory (11.1).
Tables hicut44 / locut44: the M-Band band-filter words at 44.1 kHz (section 14.7), same layout as hicut / locut.

Rest convention (17.2): patches from MIDI sources (and source none) have no value after power-up and leave the stored value (16.1); effective values follow the exact patch law of 4.10 (destination resolution: some are fractional) and add when several patches share a destination ("patches (sum)").
Every effect voice is given with its gate open (16.4); where Clear = 1 at rest, the gated level / feedback words are 0.
AutoInfinite (program 46): tank k in the notation of 15.1 (whole coefficients); k / A give the rest state (Infinite = 1), k_infinite0 / A_infinite0 the running state.

All 200 programs. The 34 programs tabulated in Part I (section 7; key part1_section) carry the stored data, the Latch block and the description; their parameters in effect, modulation state, tank and input/output values are the Part I tables (modulation, tank, io = null).
Section references follow algorithms-and-programs.md (Part I 1 - 10, Part II 11 - 19).
