programs.name: Prime Blue
programs.description: **1. Prime Blue** (Chorus+Rvb, 81 BPM). A wide chorus with tempo echoes into a 2.6 s reverb. Four short voices (9–19 ms, peak sweep 55–90 samples at 1.1–2.0 Hz, slight negative feedback) make the chorus; voices 2 and 4 are long tempo echoes (20/19 and 1 beat, 781 / 742 ms) with +0.29 feedback. The LFO (0.33 Hz) swaps the two echoes between the sides (V2 pan 0→100, V4 100→0). ADJUST ("Efx/Rvb X") crossfades effect and reverb (FX Mix 0 → 100) and below 32 pulls the echoes down (level 152 → 113, feedback to none). Sw 1 (ramp, 6 beats per cycle) is triggered through a high Latch (60) on the input level and pans voices 3 and 6 across while the input stays loud; Sw 2 is set up but drives nothing. The Footpedal narrows the output (FX Width 405 → 360). Pre-delay 1/12 beat, early reflections at 1/12 and 1/8 beat.

programs.name: EkoChorus
programs.description: **2. EkoChorus** (Chorus+Rvb, 120 BPM). Chorus and two slow echoes, little reverb (1.98 s, FX mix 0.95/0.32). Voices 1–2 (25 / 33 ms, panned 30 / 70) are a deep chorus (213-sample sweep, 0.42 / 0.34 Hz); voices 4 and 5 are echoes at 356 ms (left, +0.21 feedback, swept at 0.76 Hz, so its repeats waver in pitch) and 408 ms (right, −0.23 feedback, unmodulated). Voices 3 and 6 are off. ADJUST sets FX Mix (0 … 100 over the knob).

programs.name: Wet Chorus
programs.description: **3. Wet Chorus** (Chorus+Rvb, 120 BPM). Six chorus voices at 0 ms (126-sample sweep at 0.4–1.1 Hz each, voices 1, 2, 5, 6 with +0.30 feedback, short flanged resonance), alternately panned hard left/right, into a long 6.8 s reverb. ADJUST = FX Mix (stored 38: voices 0.83, reverb 0.56).

programs.name: Wet Chorus 2
programs.description: **4. Wet Chorus 2** (Chorus+Rvb, 120 BPM). Wet Chorus with voices 1 and 2 moved to 400 ms (+0.15 feedback, hard left / right): a chorus plus a soft doubled slap-back echo, with the same 6.8 s reverb. ADJUST = FX Mix (stored 20).

programs.name: Wet Chorus 3
programs.description: **5. Wet Chorus 3** (Chorus+Rvb, 120 BPM). As Wet Chorus 2 with the echoes panned 25 / 75 and the 0-ms voices 3 / 4 hard left / right; ADJUST = FX Mix.

programs.name: Chorus Plate
programs.description: **6. Chorus Plate** (Plate, 120 BPM). A plate (3.59 s) whose four delay voices (3–9 ms, diffused, Voice Dif 51) and post-delays are swept by the triangle LFO: the LFO moves PstDly L / R in opposite directions (16 ↔ 32), scales all voice times through the Delay Master (20 … 100 %) and modulates its own rate (0.18 … 0.50 Hz), so the chorus speeds up and slows down. ADJUST ("Korus Mix") sets PstMix, the share of the post-delayed (chorused) output.

programs.name: Chorus Room
programs.description: **7. Chorus Room** (Chamber, 120 BPM). A chamber (Mid Rt via ADJUST "Decay": 0 … 60, stored 43 = 2.60 s) with no delay voices (FX Mix 100, reverb only). The chorus is the left post-delay swept by the triangle LFO (9 ↔ 27); the LFO rate follows the input level (Mono Lvl → 0.20 … 1.00 Hz), so louder playing makes a faster chorus. The AR envelope is set up (trigger Mono Lvl ≥ 49) but drives nothing.

programs.name: ChorusToRvb
programs.description: **8. ChorusToRvb** (Chorus+Rvb, 120 BPM). A chorus that gives way to the reverb as the input gets louder. Voices at 0 / 43 / 74 ms each side (Delay Master 51 %), the 74-ms voices with strong negative feedback (−0.35, −0.31), wide mixed sweeps. The input level drives FX Mix (soft 70 → loud 12, i.e. from mostly reverb to mostly chorus) and narrows FX Width at higher levels. ADJUST ("Decay") sets Mid Rt 0 … 63 (stored 25 = 1.11 s).

programs.name: Funkus Room
programs.description: **9. Funkus Room** (Chamber, 120 BPM). A 4.2 s chamber with four short delay voices (0–18 ms, panned across) that the triangle LFO sweeps in opposite directions (V1 1 ↔ 24 ms, V3 18 ↔ 2 ms, …) together with both post-delays (cosine on the left one): a strong flanging, warbling room. ADJUST sets the LFO rate (0.02 … 3.5 Hz, stored 0.29 Hz).

programs.name: Detune&Room
programs.description: **10. Detune&Room** (Plate, 125 BPM). Pitch detune by gliding delays: the four plate voices are moved by the LFO (0.20 Hz; triangle on V1 50 → 0 ms and V4 0 → 40 ms, sine / cosine on V2 / V3 between 10 and 40 ms) and glide toward their targets, which shifts their pitch slightly up and down. ADJUST sets the glide response GldResp (0 … 100; slower glide = smoother, smaller detune). Reverb 2.76 s, FX mix 0.59 / 0.81.

programs.name: Detune&Dbl
programs.description: **11. Detune&Dbl** (Plate, 125 BPM). Detune as Detune&Room (program 10) on voices 1 and 4 only, plus voices 2 / 3 as a fixed 62-ms doubling hard left / right; short 0.60 s plate. ADJUST = GldResp.

programs.name: Tight Space
programs.description: **12. Tight Space** (Plate, 120 BPM). A small, short plate (1.31 s, Size 7) with a doubling: voices 2 / 3 at 34 ms hard left / right and voices 1 / 4 moved by the LFO (triangle, 0.33 Hz) in opposite directions (0 … 11 ms). ADJUST ("SplitWide") stretches all voice times (Delay Master 0 … 200 %) and pans voices 1 / 4 apart (50 → 0 / 100).

programs.name: Flange>Rvb
programs.description: **13. Flange>Rvb** (Glide>Hall, 117 BPM). A through-zero style stereo flanger into the hall: the glide taps of each side (A, B) are moved by the triangle LFO (0.10 Hz) in opposite directions (A: 0 ↔ 190, B: 0 ↔ 120 in 0.1 ms, i.e. up to 19 / 12 ms), mixed at 0.5 each with glide feedback −0.25 / −0.30 (left) and +0.25 / +0.30 (right). The echo voices pass the glide output at 0 ms (V1 left, V4 right). Hall 1.64 s. ADJUST = FX Mix.

programs.name: Flange+Rvb
programs.description: **14. Flange+Rvb** (Chorus+Rvb, 120 BPM). Six chorus voices at 0–2 ms (Delay Master 1 %) with deep sweeps (≈ 200 samples) and alternating ±0.27 feedback: a stereo flanger, voices 1–3 left, 4–6 right, into a 1.43 s reverb. ADJUST = FX Mix.

programs.name: X Eko Flange
programs.description: **15. X Eko Flange** (Glide>Hall, 81 BPM). A cross-feedback flanger with tempo echoes. The glide taps sweep up to ≈ 20 ms (sine on A, cosine on B, 0.11 Hz, left and right in opposite directions; glide output −5 dB). The echo voices 1 / 4 pass the line at 0 ms; voices 3 (3/2 beat) and 6 (5/2 beat) are not heard directly (level off) but feed each line into the other (cross feedback ≈ −0.27 / +0.27 at the stored Mstr XFbk 30), so tempo echoes bounce between the sides. ADJUST sets Mstr XFbk (0 … 100), i.e. how long the echoes last.

programs.name: Glide > Verb
programs.description: **16. Glide > Verb** (Glide>Hall, 75 BPM). Gliding taps (sine / cosine, 0.21 Hz; A up to 20 ms, B up to 14–15 ms) with glide feedback +0.19 / −0.12 give a slow chorus/flange that feeds the hall through diffused echo voices at 0 ms (Voice Dif 100). The tempo voices 3 / 6 are off. Hall 0.79 s. ADJUST = FX Mix.

programs.name: Glide X-Ekos
programs.description: **17. Glide X-Ekos** (Glide>Hall, 130 BPM). As Glide > Verb with the echo voices 1 / 4 at 1000 ms × Delay Master (stored 74 %: 140 ms after ADJUST) and cross feedback 0.6 between the lines: a modulated ping-pong echo. ADJUST ("Eko Time") sets the Delay Master 1 … 200 %, i.e. the echo time.

programs.name: Detuned Ekos
programs.description: **18. Detuned Ekos** (Plate, 80 BPM). Two echoes, left voice 1 and right voice 3, both at a tempo fraction chosen with ADJUST ("Ekos/Beat", 1 … 24 echoes per beat; stored 3 = 1/3 beat = 250 ms) and with negative feedback (−0.12). The LFO (0.10 Hz) stretches all voice times by up to 7 % (Delay Master 100 → 107) and swaps the post-delays (46 ↔ 0), detuning the repeats. Short plate (0.54 s), diffused voices (Voice Dif 75).

programs.name: StereoEqEkos
programs.description: **19. StereoEqEkos** (M-Band+Rvb, 81 BPM). A six-tap tempo echo through the band filters: band delays at 1 … 6 units of a tempo fraction set by ADJUST ("Ekos/Beat", 1 … 24 per beat; stored 3 → 247 ms steps) with levels falling 5 dB per tap and the taps panned alternately left (1, 2, 3) and right (4, 5, 6) toward the centre. All bands share the master filters (HiCut 83, LoCut 29); bands 3 and 6 feed back at −0.14. Reverb off (FX mix 1.00/0.00).

programs.name: ADJUpMyEchos
programs.description: **20. ADJUpMyEchos** (Concert Hall, 61 BPM). A 3.1 s hall with four tempo echoes (1 beat left, 2 beats right, 1/2 and 1/4 beat inside) with slight positive feedback (+0.07 … +0.14). ADJUST ("EchosLvl", 0 … 10) brings the echoes in: Levels Master 0 → 40; at the stored 0 the echoes are silent and only the hall (with tempo reflections at 1/4 and 1/2 beat) sounds.

programs.name: FSw2 Elevate
programs.description: **21. FSw2 Elevate** (Plate, 75 BPM). An echo that speeds up from a footswitch. The AR patches (tempo-coded, 16.6) replace the stored tempo values of voices 1 (left) and 3 (right): at rest both are 1 beat (800 ms; with −0.4 feedback after the master, diffused by Voice Dif 100, reverb out of the mix). Foot Sw 2 triggers the AR envelope (attack 64 steps ≈ 1.3 s, release 61 steps), which divides both times step by step down to 1/12 beat (66 ms; the denominator runs 1 → 12 with the envelope), raises the feedback master to 80, narrows the image (FX Width 405 → 315) and lowers the input slightly; releasing the switch reverses it. ADJUST sets the feedback master (0 … 99, stored 45). The LFO (0.10 Hz) stretches the voices by up to 7 % and swaps the post-delays as in Detuned Ekos (program 18). Sw 1 (ramp, triggered by Foot Sw 1) is set up but drives nothing.

programs.name: Chorus&Pan
programs.description: **22. Chorus&Pan** (Chorus+Rvb, 120 BPM). A chorus (voices at 0 / 3 / 5 ms each side, small depth, fast rates ≈ 1.9 Hz, slight negative feedback) auto-panned by the triangle LFO across the full width (Panning Master 0 ↔ 100). ADJUST ("LFO Rate") sets both the chorus rate (MstRate 6 … 107 %) and the pan rate (0.08 … 3.74 Hz). Reverb 1.31 s, not in the mix (FX mix 1.00/0.00).

programs.name: Chorus&Amb
programs.description: **23. Chorus&Amb** (Chorus+Rvb, 120 BPM). A chorus with ambience: six voices at 12–22 ms with strong negative feedback (−0.1 … −0.2 after the master), slowly auto-panned (triangle, one cycle per 3 beats, 25 ↔ 75) into a 2.2 s reverb (FX mix 0.81/0.59). ADJUST ("MstChorus") sets the chorus rate (MstRate 6 … 150 %) and, above 50, the depth (MstDepth 86 → 125).

programs.name: 6 Vox Chorus
programs.description: **24. 6 Vox Chorus** (Chorus+Rvb, 120 BPM). Six chorus voices at 12, 18, … 42 ms spread from left to right, positive feedback (≈ +0.1), voices only (reverb 1.72 s but FX mix 1.00/0.00). ADJUST ("Less/More", 0 … 50) raises depth (MstDepth 15 → 85) and rate (MstRate 80 → 150 %) together.

programs.name: Split C&E
programs.description: **25. Split C&E** (Chorus+Rvb, 112 BPM). Chorus on one input, echoes on the other: line A (left input) has three chorus voices (1 / 3 / 36 ms, increasing depth, slow rates 0.1–0.2 Hz), line B (right input) has three tempo echoes (1, 1/2 and 1/4 beat, panned right, little modulation, feedback −0.19 / +0.16 / −0.16). ADJUST ("Input Pan") swaps the inputs between the two lines (InPan L 0 → 100, InPan R 100 → 0). Reverb not in the mix.

programs.name: Env:PanKorus
programs.description: **26. Env:PanKorus** (Chorus+Rvb, 120 BPM). A chorus (voices 1–33 ms, small depth, ≈ 1.5 Hz, alternating ±0.2 feedback) whose output is panned by the sine LFO (15 ↔ 85); the LFO rate follows an AR envelope triggered by the input (Mono Lvl ≥ 36; attack 5 steps, release 56 steps): the pan speeds up from 0.21 Hz to several Hz while playing loud and slows down over ≈ 1.1 s after. ADJUST ("Chorus") scales chorus rate (0 … 200 %) and depth (33 … 166).

programs.name: 6 Vox Flange
programs.description: **27. 6 Vox Flange** (Chorus+Rvb, 120 BPM). Six flanger voices at 0–2 ms with deep sweeps (≈ 200 samples) and alternating ±0.3 feedback (masters 74 %), three left and three right in alternation, into a 1.3 s reverb. ADJUST sets the depth (MstDepth 0 … 200, stored 70).

programs.name: Mod Max
programs.description: **28. Mod Max** (Chamber, 120 BPM). Everything moves with one LFO (0.25 Hz, rate set by ADJUST "Mod Knob" 0.10 … 5.0 Hz): the delay voices (V1 27 ↔ 42 ms, V2 17 ↔ 5 ms, V3 0 ↔ 7 ms; V3 / V4 nearly inverted at full level), the input panning (triangle swaps InPan L / R), the reverb width (sawtooth 315 ↔ 405) and the output width (cosine 429 ↔ 291). The sawtooth also flips the LFO shape between sine and cosine once per cycle. Chamber 2.45 s, FX mix 0.71/0.71, voice feedback ±0.2.

programs.name: PreciseGlide
programs.description: **29. PreciseGlide** (Glide>Hall, 97 BPM). A slow, tempo-locked stereo glide: the LFO (triangle, one cycle per 8 beats) moves the four glide taps in opposite directions over 0 … 6 / 8 ms, mixed at about −3 dB. ADJUST ("Resonance") turns the glide feedback from none (stored) to Fbk L +0.24, Fbk R −0.24 with the cross feedback removed, giving a resonant, pitched flange. The echo voices pass the glide output (0 ms, delay master 0). Sw 1 / Sw 2 and Env L are set up but drive nothing. Hall 1.72 s.

programs.name: Round 147
programs.description: **30. Round 147** (Chorus+Rvb, 120 BPM). A rotary-speaker imitation: six short voices (1–5 ms) with fast chorus (≈ 2 Hz × MstRate) and mixed ±0.2 feedback, plus the LFO (cosine) panning the output 25 ↔ 75 and the sine narrowing the width 405 ↔ 315 at the same rate (0.9 Hz stored). ADJUST ("RotorRate", 0 … 20) sets both the rotor rate (LFO 0.26 … 6.97 Hz) and the chorus rate (MstRate 25 … 200 %).

programs.name: FSw2 Rotary
programs.description: **31. FSw2 Rotary** (Chorus+Rvb, 120 BPM). A rotary speaker with slow/fast switching from Foot Sw 2: the switch goes through a Latch (high 33), so each press toggles. The latched value triggers the AR envelope (attack 83 steps ≈ 1.7 s, release 56 steps ≈ 1.1 s), which ramps the rotor (LFO 0.40 → 6.0 Hz), the chorus rate (30 → 175 %) and depth (60 → 125) and reduces the LFO depth, like a motor speeding up and down. The LFO pans the output 0 ↔ 100 and sweeps the High Cut (91 ↔ 113). Voices at 2 / 5 / 11 ms (Delay Master 1 %), V1 / V4 with ∓0.5 feedback. ADJUST sets FX Width (315 … 405). Without a footswitch the rotor stays slow.

programs.name: RotorCabinet
programs.description: **32. RotorCabinet** (Chorus+Rvb, 120 BPM). As FSw2 Rotary, switched by the ADJUST knob instead (0 = slow, 1 = fast: the AR is triggered while ADJUST ≥ 1). A Latch on Foot Sw 1 is defined but nothing uses it.

programs.name: MIDI Rotary
programs.description: **33. MIDI Rotary** (Chorus+Rvb, 111 BPM). As FSw2 Rotary, switched by MIDI aftertouch through the Latch (high 33), with a shorter reverb (0.45 s) and tempo echoes in the reverb (EkoDly 1/3 and 1/4 beat). ADJUST lowers the echo feedback (EkoFbk 15 → 0).

programs.name: Tiled Rotary
programs.description: **34. Tiled Rotary** (Chorus+Rvb, 120 BPM). RotorCabinet (ADJUST 0 / 1 = slow / fast) with longer voice times (28 / 70 / 154 ms, Delay Master 14 %) and a 0.94 s room in the mix (0.89/0.45).

programs.name: RotoWood
programs.description: **35. RotoWood** (Chorus+Rvb, 120 BPM). A small rotary sound without reverb: voices at 2–5 ms (Delay Master 10 %), the LFO (2.22 Hz stored) pans 20 ↔ 80 and widens 380 ↔ 410. ADJUST ("Speed", 0 … 10) sets rotor rate (0.49 … 6.7 Hz), chorus depth (45 → 119) and rate (83 → 174 %). The AR (triggered through a Latch on Foot Sw 1) drives nothing.

programs.name: RandomImages
programs.description: **36. RandomImages** (Chorus+Rvb, 120 BPM). Six voices with deep, slow chorus (MstDepth 200) whose pans are moved by the LFO; the LFO rate follows the input level through a jagged curve (silence → 2.17 Hz, any signal → almost stopped, loud → 0.03–0.05 Hz), so the image jumps when the input starts. Voices 3 and 6 are tempo echoes (2 and 4 beats × Delay Master) with feedback +0.76 / −0.9. ADJUST ("ImageKnob") walks through a set of combinations: delay master, chorus depth, voice-3/6 feedback and output level change along multi-point curves.

programs.name: Under Water
programs.description: **37. Under Water** (M-Band+Rvb, 120 BPM). Band echoes (200 / 70 ms each side, +0.1 … +0.4 feedback) whose master filters are swept by the sine LFO at audio-like rates (11 Hz stored; ADJUST "DrownKnob" 10 … 25 Hz): High Cut 106 ↔ 161 and Low Cut 157 ↔ 206 move together, a bubbling, gargling sound. Long reverb (7.7 s), FX mix 0.89/0.45.

programs.name: Thunder FX
programs.description: **38. Thunder FX** (M-Band+Rvb, 125 BPM). Six tempo-locked band echoes (from 1/7 to 24/23 beat, alternating feedback −0.3 … +0.5) behind master filters driven by the AR envelope in Repeat mode: every time the input passes Mono Lvl 31 the envelope jumps open (attack 0) and closes over AR Release (stored 440 steps ≈ 8.8 s), so the filters open fully (High Cut 0 → 121, Low Cut 223 → 122) and then darken slowly, a flash followed by rumble. ADJUST ("FlashTime") sets the release (0 … 500 steps). Reverb 2.1 s, FX mix 0.99/0.13.

programs.name: Thunder FX 2
programs.description: **39. Thunder FX 2** (M-Band+Rvb, 125 BPM). Thunder FX with all band times doubled (Delay Master 200 %), a longer third band (8/5 beat), the output narrowed by the envelope (FX Width 360 → 405 on the flash), reverb out of the mix and a short stored release (ADJUST 4 → 15 steps).

programs.name: ChaosImpuls
programs.description: **40. ChaosImpuls** (Plate, 120 BPM). Four delay voices swept over very long ranges by the triangle LFO (0.11 Hz): V1 1365 → 0 ms, V4 0 → 1365 ms, V2 0 → 715 ms, V3 523 → 0 ms, gliding (GldResp, GldRange 341) so their repeats (feedback +0.16, V1 / V4 −0.5) sweep in pitch, diffused (Voice Dif 100). ADJUST sets the glide response. Plate 4.5 s.

programs.name: DemonDescent
programs.description: **41. DemonDescent** (Chorus+Rvb, 120 BPM). Very slow, very deep chorus voices (MstDepth 200, MstRate 6 %) with their delay times swept by the LFO (sawtooth 0.13 Hz: V1 0 → 1365 ms, V4 0 → 493 ms; triangle: V2 517 ↔ 274 ms, V6 133 ↔ 843 ms) and gliding: continuously falling and rising pitch. Feedback ±0.3. ADJUST = GldResp. Reverb 3.1 s.

programs.name: RoughIdle FX
programs.description: **42. RoughIdle FX** (Chamber, 50 BPM). A stutter / engine-idle effect on the reverb input: Sw 1 (ramp, 7.3 Hz stored; ADJUST "Speed" 1.5 … 10 Hz), triggered while the input is above Mono Lvl 24, chops the input level (96 ↔ 160), pans the input across and moves both post-delays and PstMix in each cycle. Only the chamber is heard (FX Mix 100, 2.2 s). The AR (Repeat) is triggered too but drives nothing.

programs.name: RoxStutter
programs.description: **43. RoxStutter** (Chorus+Rvb, 120 BPM). A chorus (voices 3–33 ms) plus two echo voices (770 / 884 ms, +0.31 feedback) whose delay follows the input envelope: Env L / Env R (release 60 steps = 1.2 s) pull the echo time down to 97 / 83 ms while the input is loud and let it glide back up as it decays, so echoes stutter and swoop. ADJUST = FX Mix.

programs.name: Split Pitch?
programs.description: **44. Split Pitch?** (Plate, 120 BPM). Two gliding delay voices, hard left (V1 1365 → 0 ms) and hard right (V4 0 → 1365 ms), swept in opposite directions by the LFO (0.21 Hz) with feedback −1 × master 0 (none): the two sides glide in pitch in opposite directions. ADJUST ("SplitWide") raises LFO depth (0 … 100) and rate (0.20 … 0.50 Hz) and the Delay Master (0 … 200 %), so at 0 there is no split. No reverb (Mid Rt 0, FX Mix 0).

programs.name: TryTalk'n
programs.description: **45. TryTalk'n** (Plate, 120 BPM). ChaosImpuls with the triangle LFO at 0.21 Hz on V1 / V4 and the sawtooth on V2 / V3, no voice feedback: gliding, talking pitch sweeps. ADJUST = GldResp.

programs.name: AutoInfinite
programs.description: **46. AutoInfinite** (Infinite, 120 BPM). An automatic freeze: the AR envelope, triggered while the input is above Mono Lvl 64 (attack and release 0 = instantly), sets the tank's Infinite switch off while playing and on as soon as the input drops, so the last sound is held indefinitely (16 s decay otherwise); new loud input releases it. Delay voices 19 / 18 ms (LFO-modulated slightly, +0.32 feedback) and 1-beat voices 2 / 3 (−0.37 feedback) and LFO-swept post-delays add movement. ADJUST = FX Mix (stored 70).

programs.name: Remove Cntr
programs.description: **47. Remove Cntr** (M-Band+Rvb, 120 BPM). Centre-channel removal: band 1 passes the left input and band 6 the right input inverted (level 0 = −1), both at 0 ms and panned to the middle, so the output is L − R and anything panned to the centre cancels. ADJUST ("Cntr Fc") raises the low cut of the inverted band (V6 LoCut 0 … 121) so that the centre is removed only above that frequency (bass and kick stay). No reverb, no feedback.

programs.name: V-Eliminate
programs.description: **48. V-Eliminate** (M-Band+Rvb, 120 BPM). Vocal elimination: both inputs pass straight (bands 1 and 4) and an inverted band-passed copy of each (bands 3 and 6, HiCut 117, LoCut 10, levels −1) is added on the other side, cancelling the centre only inside the pass band. ADJUST ("Cut Zone") narrows the band (LoCut 10 → 49, HiCut 117 → 92).

programs.name: NoCenter Eko
programs.description: **49. NoCenter Eko** (M-Band+Rvb, 143 BPM). Remove Cntr applied to a tempo echo: all four bands at 1/2 beat, the straight ones with −0.08 feedback and the inverted ones with +0.08 (after the 40 % master), master high cut 92: the echoes repeat only the side (L − R) content. ADJUST = V3 / V6 low cut as in Remove Cntr (program 47).

programs.name: Rvb On L-R
programs.description: **50. Rvb On L-R** (Res1>Plate, 214 BPM). A reverb on the side signal only, using the resonator algorithm without resonance: the six resonators are unassigned (feedback 0) and act only as their loop low-pass. Input voices 1 and 4 pass the left and right input at the centre, voices 3 and 6 add the left input inverted on the right and the right input inverted on the left, so the plate (which in this algorithm is fed by the resonator section) receives ±(L − R)/2: centre-panned sources get no reverb. FX Mix 100 = reverb only. ADJUST ("Decay") sets Mid Rt 0 … 63 (stored 46 = 3.1 s). Reverb echoes at 1/6 and 1/4 beat.

programs.name: [n]Ekos/Beat
programs.description: **51. [n]Ekos/Beat** (Plate, 81 BPM). A stereo echo whose rate is chosen in echoes per beat: ADJUST ("[n]", 1 … 24) sets voice 1 (left), voice 3 (right) and the pre-delay to 1/n beat together (stored 2: 1/2 beat = 371 ms), with slight negative feedback (−0.12). The plate (1.31 s) is mostly out of the mix (FX mix 0.99/0.13). The LFO has depth 0.

programs.name: StereoTapDly
programs.description: **52. StereoTapDly** (M-Band+Rvb, 81 BPM). Two 1-beat echoes (742 ms), band 1 hard left and band 4 hard right, with a dark master high cut (95) and feedback −1 × the master: ADJUST ("Mstr Fbk", 0 … 100, stored 20) sets the number of repeats. A triangle LFO (8 beats per cycle) is patched to swap the pans but its depth is 0, so the echoes stay put. No reverb.

programs.name: OffBeat Eko
programs.description: **53. OffBeat Eko** (M-Band+Rvb, 81 BPM). Off-beat echoes: band 1 left at 3/4 beat × 50 % (278 ms) and band 4 right at 3/2 beat × 50 % (556 ms), feedback −0.1, dark tape-like filtering (LoCut 17, master LoCut 138). ADJUST ("DarkKnob") sets the master high cut 0 … 240 (stored 85). Band 5 (1/4 beat) is set but off. No reverb in the mix.

programs.name: OffBeatEko2
programs.description: **54. OffBeatEko2** (M-Band+Rvb, 81 BPM). OffBeat Eko with two extra quieter taps (−6 dB): band 2 at 1/2 beat × 50 % (185 ms, left) and band 5 at 1/4 beat × 50 % (92 ms, right), all with tiny feedback; a denser off-beat pattern. ADJUST = master high cut.

programs.name: Dotted 8ths
programs.description: **55. Dotted 8ths** (M-Band+Rvb, 80 BPM). A six-tap rhythm in dotted eighths: taps at 3/4, 4/4, 6/4, 7/4, 9/4 and 10/4 beat (563 ms … 1.88 s) spread across the stereo field, each 4–5 dB quieter than the one before, from a mono input (InPan 50 / 50); the feedback master is 0 (no repeats). ADJUST ("EchoSlope") tilts the level slope: at 0 the first tap is loudest, at 127 the last (rising echoes). No reverb.

programs.name: Shuffle Ekos
programs.description: **56. Shuffle Ekos** (M-Band+Rvb, 81 BPM). A shuffle (triplet) echo: taps at 2, 3, 5, 6, 8 and 9 thirds of a beat × 50 %, the on-beat taps (1, 3, 5) at −3 dB and the shuffle taps (2, 4, 6) at −22 dB at the stored knob. ADJUST ("Shufl Lvl") crossfades between the two groups (0: shuffle taps loud, main taps down; 127: the reverse).

programs.name: Shuffles
programs.description: **57. Shuffles** (M-Band+Rvb, 120 BPM). The shuffle tap pattern at full length (2/3 … 3 beats, 333 ms … 1.5 s) with a falling slope (0 … −24 dB). ADJUST ("EchoSlope") sets how steeply taps 2–6 fall (0: steep, down to off; 100: all equal).

programs.name: Sliding Eko
programs.description: **58. Sliding Eko** (Plate, 80 BPM). Two 1-beat echoes (voices 1 left, 3 right; feedback master 0, so single repeats) with a 1-beat reflection pair in a very short plate. ADJUST ("Slide It!") moves the Delay Master 50 … 150 % (stored 75 % = 562 ms); turning it makes the echoes glide in pitch while their delay slides. FX mix 0.71/0.71.

programs.name: Six Trips
programs.description: **59. Six Trips** (M-Band+Rvb, 94 BPM). Six taps at 1/4, 2/4 … 6/4 beat (159 … 957 ms), panned across, rising in level from −10 to −3 dB at the stored knob; ADJUST ("EchoSlope") tilts the slope as in Dotted 8ths. No reverb.

programs.name: 6 StrokeRoll
programs.description: **60. 6 StrokeRoll** (M-Band+Rvb, 86 BPM). A drum-roll build-up: five taps at 1/4 … 5/4 beat × 33 % (57 … 288 ms; tap 6 is off) rising from −19 to −5 dB, a crescendo of strokes after each hit. ADJUST ("Attack") tilts the slope (stored 85: rising). No reverb.

programs.name: TapGated Rvb
programs.description: **61. TapGated Rvb** (Chamber, 81 BPM). A tempo-gated chamber: the LFO (pulse, 2 beats per cycle, short pulse width 12) switches the reverb input (Rvb In) between off and the level set by ADJUST, so the chamber (2.3 s) is fed only during a short window at the start of every 2 beats; reverb only (FX Mix 100), tempo echoes and reflections in the tank (1/3 and 2/3 beat). ADJUST ("Gate dB") sets the open level (Rvb In 80 → 1, i.e. 0 to −79 dB).

programs.name: TapEkoGate 1
programs.description: **62. TapEkoGate 1** (M-Band+Rvb, 81 BPM). The OffBeatEko2 pattern (3/4, 1/2, 3/2, 1/4 beat; feedback +0.2 / −0.14) behind a tempo gate on the input: the LFO (pulse, 4 beats per cycle, width 86) pulls the input level from 160 down toward 81 (off) for most of each 4-beat cycle. ADJUST ("GateWidth") sets the LFO depth (0 = no gating, stored 47 = partial). Sw 1 / Sw 2 (pulse, 4 beats) are set up but drive nothing. Reverb out of the mix.

programs.name: TapEkoGate 2
programs.description: **63. TapEkoGate 2** (M-Band+Rvb, 81 BPM). As TapEkoGate 1 with other tap times (1/2, 3/2, 1/2, 3/4 beat) and the gate patched from Sw 1 (pulse, 4 beats per cycle, width by ADJUST 0 … 98). Sw 1's trigger is "none ≥ 1", which by 6.3 never triggers, so the switch stays at its idle 0 (input open) unless it is restarted from outside (the Tap key restarts the time switches). FX mix 0.99/0.16.

programs.name: TapEkoClear
programs.description: **64. TapEkoClear** (M-Band+Rvb, 81 BPM). The TapEkoGate 1 echoes with more feedback (master 71: +0.30 / −0.22), cleared rhythmically: the LFO pulse (4 beats per cycle) drives the Clear switch, which holds the band input levels (16.4) while the pulse is low, so the lines empty out, and lets the echoes build up again when it is high. ADJUST ("GateWidth") sets the pulse width (stored 78 %). At rest (LFO output 0) the lines are cleared. FX mix 0.89/0.45.

programs.name: Tap Chamber1
programs.description: **65. Tap Chamber1** (Chamber, 81 BPM). A short chamber (0.42 s) with two early voices (17 ms left, 29 ms right) whose colour moves with the tempo: Sw 1 (ramp, 4 beats per cycle, always running) sweeps Rt HC (10 → 34), Crossover and the Shape (10 → 149) once every 4 beats. ADJUST sets the reverb width (360 … 450).

programs.name: Tap Chamber2
programs.description: **66. Tap Chamber2** (Chamber, 81 BPM). A long chamber (6.8 s, Size 127) with four early voices (5–15 ms) and tempo echoes in the tank (3/4 and 12/15 beat). Sw 1 (ramp, 4 beats) breathes the reverb width (360 ↔ 460); the input level triggers the AR (Mono Lvl ≥ 46, attack 3, release 50 steps), which skews the echo feedback (left down to 9, right up to 21) while playing. ADJUST ("Decay") sets the Shape 0 … 254.

programs.name: LatchedEkos
programs.description: **67. LatchedEkos** (M-Band+Rvb, 81 BPM). Two echo pairs that take turns in tempo: 1/2-beat echoes (bands 1 / 4, feedback −0.28) and 1/3-beat echoes (bands 3 / 6, +0.52). The LFO pulse (4 beats per cycle, width by ADJUST "EchoWidth") gates the input (81 ↔ 160) and also feeds a Latch (low 11, high 110) that triggers the AR envelope (attack / release 5 steps); the AR crossfades the levels between the pairs (V1 / V4 up, V3 / V6 down). No reverb.

programs.name: X-PanEQ BPM
programs.description: **68. X-PanEQ BPM** (M-Band+Rvb, 97 BPM). Tempo auto-pan of the inputs through two band filters: bands 1 and 4 pass the left and right lines at 0 ms with different band-pass settings (HiCut 80 / 87, LoCut 69 / 62); the sine and cosine of the LFO (2/3 beat per cycle) pan each input across, so the two filtered colours circle the stereo field in time. ADJUST ("Low Tone") sets the master low cut (61 … 121). Short reverb in the background (0.76 s, 0.98/0.22).

programs.name: Pan>Eko BPM
programs.description: **69. Pan>Eko BPM** (M-Band+Rvb, 120 BPM). The inputs are panned by the LFO (sine, 2/3 beat per cycle) before dark echoes: band 2 / 5 dry at 0 ms and band 1 / 4 at 200 ms (Delay Master 20 %, −6 dB, HiCut 112, feedback −0.53). ADJUST ("DarkKnob") = master high cut 0 … 121. Reverb 1.31 s at 0.41.

programs.name: Tempo Verb
programs.description: **70. Tempo Verb** (Chamber, 97 BPM). A chamber whose decay follows the Tempo source (16.1): source 0 → Mid Rt 56 (7.7 s), 127 → 1; with no tempo value supplied the decay stays at 56. ADJUST ("Liveness") raises the reflections (RefLvl 0 → 15), Spread (43 → 255) and Rt HC (14 → 45) together. Reverb only.

programs.name: Tempo Gate
programs.description: **71. Tempo Gate** (Inverse, 110 BPM). An inverse/gated reverb whose length follows the Tempo source (Duration 112 → 32 → 0 over source 0 … 30 … 100; stored 44). The four short voices (20–36 ms) are at −40 dB (Levels Master 0) and FX Mix is 100, so only the reverb is heard. ADJUST sets the High Cut (68 … 118).

programs.name: Tape Echo
programs.description: **72. Tape Echo** (M-Band+Rvb, 80 BPM). A dark tape echo: band 1 left and band 4 right at 1/2 beat (375 ms) with +0.42 feedback through LoCut 17 and the master filters (HiCut 85, LoCut 138), so each repeat gets darker and thinner. ADJUST ("DarkKnob") sets the master high cut 0 … 240. No reverb in the mix.

programs.name: NonLinear 1
programs.description: **73. NonLinear 1** (Chorus+Rvb, 80 BPM). A shaped echo burst from the chorus voices used as plain delays: six voices at 1/2 … 6/2 beat × 50 % (188 … 563 ms), no modulation (MstDepth 0), panned around, with an ADJUST level curve ("EchoSlope"): at 64 all equal, toward 127 a rising slope (last voice loudest, like a reversed decay), toward 0 a falling slope. No reverb.

programs.name: NonLinear 2
programs.description: **74. NonLinear 2** (Chorus+Rvb, 176 BPM). NonLinear 1 at 176 BPM (85 … 511 ms) with some chorus movement (MstDepth 50, slow MstRate 17 %), pre-delay 1/8 beat and a little reverb (0.9 s, FX mix 0.95/0.31).

programs.name: NonLinear 3
programs.description: **75. NonLinear 3** (Chorus+Rvb, 111 BPM). The shuffle pattern (2/3 … 3 beats × 25 %: 90 … 270 ms) on the chorus voices with slight movement (MstDepth 50, MstRate 38 %), from a mono input; ADJUST level slope as NonLinear 1.

programs.name: Six Across
programs.description: **76. Six Across** (M-Band+Rvb, 120 BPM). Six band echoes spaced 120 ms apart (120 … 720 ms) and panned from right (longest) to left (shortest), each in its own frequency band (bass at 120 ms … treble at 720 ms); the feedback master is 0 (single repeats). ADJUST ("Spacing") scales all times (Delay Master 0 … 200 %). No reverb.

programs.name: BandEko Rvb
programs.description: **77. BandEko Rvb** (M-Band+Rvb, 143 BPM). A band-pass echo: bands 1 / 4 at 1 beat (419 ms) with −0.5 feedback, through master filters that ADJUST ("Center Fc") moves together (HiCut 0 → 120, LoCut 122 → 240): a sweepable band-pass centre. Reverb 1.2 s with tempo echoes at 3/2 beat, pre-delay 1/2 beat.

programs.name: BandEkoSweep
programs.description: **78. BandEkoSweep** (M-Band+Rvb, 120 BPM). Three echo times (1/2, 1 and 3/2 beat) per side; the 1/2- and 3/2-beat bands have their filters swept by the time switches (Sw 1 ramp 0.15 Hz on bands 1 / 4, Sw 2 ramp 0.27 Hz on bands 3 / 6), left and right in opposite directions, so the repeats sweep through the spectrum; the LFO breathes the output width (315 ↔ 405). Feedback +0.8 / +0.4 / −0.4 × master (ADJUST "Mstr Fbk", stored 46). No reverb.

programs.name: LFO EQ Echo
programs.description: **79. LFO EQ Echo** (M-Band+Rvb, 80 BPM). 1/2-beat echoes (375 ms, −0.5 feedback) through master filters swept by the LFO in tempo (4/3 beat per cycle): the low cut follows the sine (121 ↔ 205), the high cut the cosine (100 ↔ 146). ADJUST ("LC Depth") = LFO depth. Reverb 1.9 s at 0.31.

programs.name: ChaseEcho
programs.description: **80. ChaseEcho** (M-Band+Rvb, 80 BPM). LFO EQ Echo with 1-beat echoes whose pans are patched from Sw 1 (ramp, rate by ADJUST "ChaseRate" 0 … 5 Hz). Sw 1's trigger is "none ≥ 30", which never triggers (6.3), so at rest both echoes sit at the left; the chase runs only when the switch is restarted from outside.

programs.name: Panned Dlys
programs.description: **81. Panned Dlys** (M-Band+Rvb, 125 BPM). Two echoes, 1 beat (480 ms, feedback −0.1) and 1/2 beat (240 ms, feedback −0.5), auto-panned by the triangle LFO (0.25 Hz) in opposite directions. ADJUST = feedback master. No reverb.

programs.name: X-Pan Delays
programs.description: **82. X-Pan Delays** (M-Band+Rvb, 176 BPM). Two 1-beat echoes (340 ms) crossing in the stereo field (triangle LFO, 0.25 Hz, opposite directions), feedback −0.25 at the stored ADJUST ("Mstr Fbk"). No reverb.

programs.name: Dly>EQ>Pans
programs.description: **83. Dly>EQ>Pans** (M-Band+Rvb, 333 BPM). Two filtered echoes, a dark low band at 2 beats (left, HiCut 65, LoCut 36, feedback −0.6) and a brighter band at 3 beats (right, HiCut 105, LoCut 55, feedback −0.36), i.e. 360 and 540 ms at the stored 333 BPM (16.3), auto-panned in opposite directions (triangle 0.25 Hz). ADJUST = feedback master. No reverb.

programs.name: Ekoz 4 Drums
programs.description: **84. Ekoz 4 Drums** (Plate, 115 BPM). A drum ambience with moving echoes: four diffused voices (Voice Dif 90) at 25–92 ms (× 144 %) with feedback (+0.1, +0.05), slowly modulated (0.09 Hz) by sine, triangle and cosine together with both post-delays; a 1.5 s plate with tempo echoes and reflections at 1/4 and 3/13 beat. ADJUST = FX Mix (stored 70).

programs.name: Haas PanKnob
programs.description: **85. Haas PanKnob** (Plate, 125 BPM). Panning by time difference (Haas effect) of a mono input: voice 1 hard left and voice 3 hard right at full level, voices only (FX Mix 0). ADJUST ("L=0,R=127") delays one side by up to 2 ms (below 64 the right voice, above 64 the left one; 64 = centre), with the fastest glide (GldResp 100) so the knob moves smoothly. The plate is not heard.

programs.name: Dial a Delay
programs.description: **86. Dial a Delay** (M-Band+Rvb, 80 BPM). A simple stereo echo whose time is "dialled": bands 1 / 4 at 1250 ms × Delay Master, ADJUST ("Delay") sets the master 0 … 200 % (stored 30 % = 375 ms); feedback −0.25. Reverb out of the mix.

programs.name: PrecisionDly
programs.description: **87. PrecisionDly** (Glide>Hall, 117 BPM). A precise sub-millisecond delay between the channels: glide tap A of each side at full level, the left one set by ADJUST ("L ms/100") from 0 to 1.0 ms in 0.1-ms steps (tap positions in 1/4096 sample, gliding). No feedback, no reverb. Several modulators are set (LFO, Env L, Sw 1, Sw 2) but nothing is patched from them.

programs.name: PhoneOrRoom?
programs.description: **88. PhoneOrRoom?** (M-Band+Rvb, 120 BPM). A two-way switch on ADJUST ("Pick One", 0 / 1). At 0 the six bands pass the inputs at 0 ms through a narrow telephone band (master HiCut 74, master LoCut 200) with a narrowed image (FX Width 360) and no reverb; at 1 FX Mix goes to 100 and only a small, short room is heard (Size 5, 1.1 s) at full width.

programs.name: CheapTV Room
programs.description: **89. CheapTV Room** (M-Band+Rvb, 120 BPM). The telephone band (HiCut 80, master LoCut 202) collapsed to the centre (all pans 50) plus a tiny boxy room (0.29 s, Size 2) at 0.41: a small speaker in a small room. ADJUST ("The Walls") sets the low-frequency decay (Low Rt 0 … 9).

programs.name: Empty Stage
programs.description: **90. Empty Stage** (Chamber, 120 BPM). A stage ambience: two early voices (49 ms left, 40 ms right) and a chamber whose liveness is set by ADJUST: Mid Rt 0 … 39 (stored 0.86 s), Crossover, Shape (10 … 206) and High Cut (97 … 114) together. FX mix 0.23/0.97.

programs.name: Tomb Room
programs.description: **91. Tomb Room** (M-Band+Rvb, 120 BPM). A stone room: reverb only (FX Mix 100, the bands at −12 dB are not heard), 1.89 s. ADJUST ("The Walls") makes the walls harder/softer: Low Rt 0 … 9, Rvb Out 15 → 6 and Shape 0 → 100.

programs.name: Comb Room
programs.description: **92. Comb Room** (Chorus+Rvb, 120 BPM). Static comb filtering: the chorus voices without modulation (MstDepth 0) at 0–16 ms × Delay Master, with feedback ±0.3, colour the sound like a resonant tube; ADJUST ("Tone") sets the Delay Master 0 … 200 % (stored 68 %), which tunes the comb. A 1.3 s reverb at 0.26.

programs.name: Zoom Over
programs.description: **93. Zoom Over** (Chamber, 71 BPM). Something flying over, repeating: one sawtooth LFO cycle (0.07 Hz; ADJUST "Speed" 0.01 … 0.25 Hz) raises the input level to the maximum at mid-cycle and back down (96 → 160 → 96), widens the image (360 → 450), moves both post-delays through 0 at the centre (Doppler-like pitch shift), opens the High Cut at the centre (59 → 120) and shortens the decay as it passes (Mid Rt 39 → 21 → 39). Reverb only. The AR (Repeat, trigger Mono Lvl ≥ 24) drives nothing.

programs.name: OneShotCarBy
programs.description: **94. OneShotCarBy** (Glide>Hall, 47 BPM). A car driving past, once per note: the input (above Mono Lvl 12) starts the AR envelope in One Shot mode; during the attack (ADJUST "Speed": 500 → 25 steps = 10 … 0.5 s, stored 10 s) the input is panned from left to right, its level rises to full at the middle and falls again (81 → 160 → 81), and glide tap A moves from 42 ms to 0 at the middle and back to 42 ms: the approaching car is pitched up, the receding one down (Doppler). Release 0: back to the start at once when the input stops. Hall 0.6 s. One Shot envelope: 16.2.

programs.name: AmbientCarBy
programs.description: **95. AmbientCarBy** (Chamber, 120 BPM). The car-by on a chamber (reverb only): the AR in Repeat mode (attack set by ADJUST, stored 10 s) pans the input across, swells its level and swings the post-delays (46 → 0 → 107 left, 98 → 0 → 46 right) for the Doppler shift; while the input stays above Mono Lvl 24, passes repeat. Repeat envelope: 16.2.

programs.name: HeadOn CarBy
programs.description: **96. HeadOn CarBy** (Chamber, 71 BPM). A continuous head-on pass driven by the sawtooth LFO (ADJUST "Speed" 0.10 … 2.0 Hz, stored 0.10 Hz): input level up to the middle of the cycle and down, width 360 → 450, post-delays through 0 at the centre, PstMix, FX Adjust and Mid Rt (0 → 58 → 62) all follow the cycle. The input is not panned (head-on). Reverb only.

programs.name: 2WayStreet
programs.description: **97. 2WayStreet** (Chamber, 50 BPM). Traffic both ways: Sw 1 in ramp mode (up then down; rate by ADJUST 0.10 … 2.0 Hz, stored 0.21 Hz), triggered while the input is above Mono Lvl 24, swells the input level, pans it across and back and swings the post-delays; one ramp cycle = one pass out and one back. 2.2 s chamber, reverb only.

programs.name: IntoTunnel
programs.description: **98. IntoTunnel** (Chamber, 71 BPM). Driving into a tunnel and out, repeating with the sawtooth LFO (ADJUST 0.05 … 0.50 Hz): the input swells and pans across, the post-delays swing, the High Cut opens at the middle, and the decay grows from 0 to 58 (5 s) toward the middle of the cycle. Reverb only.

programs.name: 2WayTunnel
programs.description: **99. 2WayTunnel** (Chamber, 50 BPM). 2WayStreet in a tunnel: the triangle LFO (ADJUST 0.05 … 2.0 Hz, stored 0.08 Hz) drives the pass (level, pan, post-delays, PstMix) and its cosine opens the High Cut (56 → 121) and shortens the very long decay (Mid Rt 62 → 33) in the middle of each pass.

programs.name: FinishLine
programs.description: **100. FinishLine** (Glide>Hall, 47 BPM). The OneShotCarBy pass in Repeat mode (cars keep passing while the input is above Mono Lvl 25), plus long echo voices (V3 1.59 s and V2 2.88 s left, V6 1.74 s and V5 2.88 s right after the Delay Master) that echo each pass like a grandstand. ADJUST ("Speed") shortens the echoes (Delay Master 200 → 37 %) and the pass (attack 500 → 25 steps) together. Hall 1.9 s at 0.26.

programs.name: StereoLoPass
programs.description: **101. StereoLoPass** (M-Band+Rvb, 120 BPM). A stereo low-pass filter: all six bands pass the input at 0 ms (−6 dB, three per side; feedback master 0) and ADJUST ("CutOff") sweeps the master high cut 0 … 120 (stored 56). The reverb (2.9 s) is not in the mix.

programs.name: Low Pass HiQ
programs.description: **102. Low Pass HiQ** (M-Band+Rvb, 94 BPM). A resonant low-pass: the band delays are 0 (Delay Master 0), so each band feeds back around a one-sample loop with −0.82 feedback, which peaks the response at the cutoff. ADJUST ("CutOff") sweeps the master high cut 0 … 120 and, in its top range, takes the resonance out (feedback master 100 → 90 at 90, → 0 at 127).

programs.name: Low Pass LFO
programs.description: **103. Low Pass LFO** (M-Band+Rvb, 80 BPM). The resonant low-pass swept by the LFO in tempo (triangle, 8 beats per cycle): master high cut 120 → 23 and feedback master 0 → 100 along the cycle. ADJUST ("Depth") = LFO depth (stored 89 %).

programs.name: StereoHiPass
programs.description: **104. StereoHiPass** (M-Band+Rvb, 176 BPM). A stereo high-pass: six bands at 0 ms, ADJUST ("CutOff") sweeps the master low cut 122 … 240 (stored 190); feedback master 0.

programs.name: StereoB-Pass
programs.description: **105. StereoB-Pass** (M-Band+Rvb, 120 BPM). A resonant stereo band-pass: ADJUST ("Center") moves the master high and low cut together (HiCut 0 → 120, LoCut 122 → 240), with one-sample-loop feedback (−0.5, −0.2) for a peaked response.

programs.name: Stereo Notch
programs.description: **106. Stereo Notch** (M-Band+Rvb, 120 BPM). A notch filter: the six bands are phase-inverted (levels 0) band-passes centred by ADJUST ("Center": HiCut 0 → 120, LoCut 122 → 240 together) and are added to the reverb path, which at Size 0 / Mid Rt 0 passes the signal almost directly; the inverted band cancels the centre frequency (FX Mix 60 sets the balance).

programs.name: SweptNotches
programs.description: **107. SweptNotches** (M-Band+Rvb, 300 BPM). Four inverted resonant bands at 1 ms (feedback +0.3 … +0.55) whose filters are swept continuously by the two time switches (Sw 1 ramp on bands 1 / 4, Sw 2 ramp on bands 3 / 6, left and right in opposite directions), combined with the near-direct reverb path: moving notches like a phaser. ADJUST ("Rate") sets the Sw 1 rate (0 … 1.7 Hz); Sw 2 modulates its own rate.

programs.name: Env  Notches
programs.description: **108. Env Notches** (M-Band+Rvb, 300 BPM). As SweptNotches with the filter sweeps driven by the input envelope followers (Env L on bands 1 / 4, Env R on bands 3 / 6) from a mono input: louder playing moves the notches (auto-wah style). ADJUST ("Release") sets both follower releases (0 … 50 steps).

programs.name: BandReject 4
programs.description: **109. BandReject 4** (M-Band+Rvb, 300 BPM). Four 2-ms bands with ±0.4 feedback whose filters are swept by Sw 1 / Sw 2 (ramps, 0.16 / 0.24 Hz, opposite directions per side), the output width breathing with the LFO (315 ↔ 405), into a 4.2 s reverb. ADJUST = FX Mix.

programs.name: WaaPedalEko
programs.description: **110. WaaPedalEko** (M-Band+Rvb, 120 BPM). A pedal wah: three band-passes at 0 / 4 / 0 ms (mono input) with feedback near +0.9 resonate like a wah filter; the Footpedal moves their centres (band 1 HiCut/LoCut 46 → 66, band 2 84 → 71, band 3 89 → 86) and lowers the resonance in the middle of its travel. Only the bands are heard (FX mix 1.00/0.06); the reverb holds tempo echoes (2 and 3 beats). ADJUST ("FeedBack") sets the feedback master 90 … 100. Without a pedal the stored settings apply (or those of a full pedal, 16.1).

programs.name: RotorWaa
programs.description: **111. RotorWaa** (M-Band+Rvb, 120 BPM). The wah of WaaPedalEko (program 110) moved by the sine LFO in tempo instead of the pedal, with the output panned 10 ↔ 90 by the same LFO; reverb 3.6 s at 0.79. The stored LFO Rate is 2 beats per cycle, but ADJUST ("Rate", tempo-coded patch, 16.6) replaces it: 8 beats per cycle at 0 (0.25 Hz), 5/3 beat at the stored 4 (1.20 Hz), 1/8 beat at 10 (16 Hz).

programs.name: Movable Echo
programs.description: **112. Movable Echo** (M-Band+Rvb, 67 BPM). A left echo at 1/2 beat (449 ms, +0.21 feedback) and a right echo at 1/4 beat (224 ms, +0.5), dark filtering (master HiCut 109, LoCut 138). ADJUST ("Position") sets the output width 360 … 450, moving the echoes inward or outward. Tap delays are in 32-sample steps (11.1).

programs.name: Movable Hall
programs.description: **113. Movable Hall** (Concert Hall, 120 BPM). A 2.2 s hall, nearly all reverb (FX mix 0.06/1.00), with two 80-ms voices (left / right, small negative feedback, slightly diffused). ADJUST ("Position") sets the output width 360 … 450.

programs.name: Go Away
programs.description: **114. Go Away** (Concert Hall, 120 BPM). Distance on one knob: ADJUST ("How Far?") darkens the sound (High Cut 111 → 28), raises the reverb share (FX Mix 10 → 100), the Def and Depth of the hall, the reflection levels and the reverb width, all reaching their end at 96. At 0 the dry-like 0-ms voices dominate (FX mix 0.99/0.16). Hall 3.6 s.

programs.name: Circular Pan
programs.description: **115. Circular Pan** (Chamber, 158 BPM). A sound circling the listener: the sine of the LFO pans the input (InPan L and R together), the cosine moves the "front/back" cues at the same rate (High Cut 121 → 74, reverb share FX Mix 30 → 71, width 405 → 450, level −8 at the back). ADJUST ("Rate") sets the LFO rate (0.01 … 4.0 Hz, stored 0.08 Hz). The AR, Sw 1 and Latch are set up but drive nothing.

programs.name: Spatial Hall
programs.description: **116. Spatial Hall** (Concert Hall, 136 BPM). A 2.1 s hall, reverb only, with tempo-locked reflections (1/6 and 2/9 beat) and post-delays (1/4 and 5/19 beat). ADJUST ("Position", 0 … 35) raises Depth (0 → 15) and widens the reverb (390 → 425).

programs.name: Rear of Hall
programs.description: **117. Rear of Hall** (Concert Hall, 120 BPM). A large hall heard from the back: reverb only (Size 295), High Cut 109; ADJUST ("Decay") sets Mid Rt 7 … 57 (stored 40 = 2.2 s).

programs.name: Backstage
programs.description: **118. Backstage** (Concert Hall, 120 BPM). Go Away without the reverb crossfade (reverb only): ADJUST ("How Far?") darkens the hall (High Cut 111 → 28) and raises Def, Depth and the reflections. Hall 2.45 s.

programs.name: Steered Rear
programs.description: **119. Steered Rear** (Plate, 120 BPM). A long plate (10.5 s; ADJUST "Decay" Mid Rt 51 … 61) whose position follows the playing: the AR (trigger Mono Lvl ≥ 44, attack 3, release 63 steps) brings the dry-like 0-ms voices forward while playing (FX Mix 100 → 30, PstMix 100 → 50) and narrows the reverb (450 → 375), and lets the plate come back as the input stops. The LFO (0.34 Hz) moves the post-delays and the voice times (0 … 13 / 15 ms) for slow chorusing.

programs.name: Too Deep!
programs.description: **120. Too Deep!** (Concert Hall, 120 BPM). A deep hall (Size 296; ADJUST "Decay" Mid Rt 23 … 60, stored 3.6 s) with two 0-ms voices and two echoes (409 / 433 ms, feedback ±0.2), diffused (Voice Dif 67). The input envelopes push the post-delays apart (Env R → PstDly L, Env L → PstDly R, 0 → 47) while playing, and the AR narrows the reverb.

programs.name: Dyna-Hall
programs.description: **121. Dyna-Hall** (Concert Hall, 120 BPM). A hall (Size 174; ADJUST "Decay" Mid Rt 28 … 58, stored 3.9 s) that gets wider when played loud: the AR (Mono Lvl ≥ 16, attack 10, release 64 steps) moves the reverb width 372 → 416.

programs.name: RotoRox
programs.description: **122. RotoRox** (Chorus+Rvb, 120 BPM). RoxStutter's envelope-pulled echoes (770 / 884 ms → 97 / 82 ms while loud, release 2 s) with a chorus (7–43 ms), a 12.7 s reverb and a moving width (triangle LFO 405 ↔ 315) whose rate jumps from 0.30 to 3.65 Hz while the input is loud (AR, trigger Mono Lvl ≥ 37). ADJUST = FX Mix.

programs.name: RotoRoomVox
programs.description: **123. RotoRoomVox** (Chamber, 79 BPM). A chamber (reverb only; ADJUST "Decay" Mid Rt 5 … 56) whose output width is swept by a sawtooth LFO over the whole range (0 … 720, i.e. mono through to wide and swapped), slowly (0.07 Hz) while the input is loud and fast (0.60 Hz) when it is quiet (AR, trigger Mono Lvl ≥ 43, attack 4, release 7 steps).

programs.name: RotoRoom
programs.description: **124. RotoRoom** (Chamber, 120 BPM). A chamber (ADJUST "Decay" Mid Rt 0 … 62) with the output width swept by the triangle LFO (360 ↔ 425, 0.35 Hz). The AR is set up but drives nothing.

programs.name: RotoRoom#2
programs.description: **125. RotoRoom#2** (Chamber, 120 BPM). A chamber with a rotating image: sawtooth LFO on the output width (0 … 720), sine / cosine on the two voice times (26 ↔ 41 ms; voice 1 almost fully inverted, left; voice 3 right) and the triangle moving the post-delays in opposite directions. ADJUST ("Rt & Rate") sets the decay (Mid Rt 6 … 61) and, inversely, the LFO rate (1.17 … 0.05 Hz).

programs.name: Tremolo Tap1
programs.description: **126. Tremolo Tap1** (M-Band+Rvb, 81 BPM). A tempo tremolo: the LFO (sine, 1/2 beat per cycle) moves both input levels through 160 → 120 → 160, a level dip at mid-cycle, so the tremolo runs at twice the LFO rate (four dips per beat); bands 1 / 4 pass the inputs at 0 ms (FX mix 0.99/0.16). ADJUST ("Depth") is also patched to the input levels (40 → 0).

programs.name: X-TremoloTap
programs.description: **127. X-TremoloTap** (M-Band+Rvb, 143 BPM). A stereo (alternating) tremolo: the LFO (1 beat per cycle) moves the left input 120 → 160 and the right 160 → 120, so the level swings between the sides once per beat. ADJUST ("Depth") is patched to the input levels as in Tremolo Tap1 (program 126).

programs.name: Panner  BPM
programs.description: **128. Panner BPM** (M-Band+Rvb, 61 BPM). A tempo auto-pan of the inputs (2 beats per cycle): the left input is panned by the sine, the right by the LFO output, whose shape ADJUST ("Pan Phase") selects: 1 = cosine (the two inputs circle 90° apart, stored), 0 = sine (both move together).

programs.name: Nice Pan!
programs.description: **129. Nice Pan!** (Plate, 106 BPM). A diffused plate (Voice Dif 99, 3.9 s) whose four short voices (18–38 ms, ±0.2 … 0.4 feedback) are panned as a whole by the triangle LFO (Panning Master 0 ↔ 100, 0.24 Hz) while the post-delays move with it. ADJUST = FX Mix.

programs.name: Spin & Duck
programs.description: **130. Spin & Duck** (Chorus+Rvb, 81 BPM). The rotary voices of FSw2 Rotary with the rotor speed on ADJUST ("Spin Rate": LFO 0.40 … 6.0 Hz, chorus depth 156 → 48, rate 30 → 175 %), pan and High Cut moved by the sine, and ducked echoes: the input level sets the reverb echo feedback (EkoFbk 11 when quiet → 15 = none when loud), so 1/2-beat echoes appear when the playing stops. The AR (through a Latch on Foot Sw 1) drives nothing.

programs.name: MultiFx Fade
programs.description: **131. MultiFx Fade** (Chorus+Rvb, 80 BPM). Chorus voices and short echoes (30–129 ms after the Delay Master 10 %, mixed depths, ±0.4 feedback) with an automatic swell: the AR (Mono Lvl ≥ 16, attack 7, release 34 steps) raises the input level (136 → 160), opens the High Cut (47 → 111) and swaps the pans of voices 3 and 6 while playing. ADJUST = FX Mix.

programs.name: Ghost
programs.description: **132. Ghost** (Inverse, 120 BPM). An inverse reverb (Duration 64), reverb only, whose two post-delays are moved in opposite directions by the LFO (0.14 Hz, 32 ↔ 0): a slow, ghostly flanging of the reverse swell. ADJUST ("FadeShape") sets Diffusion (0 … 100) and Shape (0 … 255) together.

programs.name: Ghost Flange
programs.description: **133. Ghost Flange** (Inverse, 120 BPM). Ghost with a longer Duration (89).

programs.name: GhostVibrato
programs.description: **134. GhostVibrato** (Inverse, 120 BPM). The inverse reverb (Duration 89) with a vibrato: the LFO (triangle, 3.72 Hz) moves both post-delays (0 → 32), and its depth is brought in by the AR while playing (Mono Lvl ≥ 12; attack 203 steps ≈ 4 s, release 15: LFO Depth 0 → 45). ADJUST ("FadeShape") as in Ghost.

programs.name: AutoFadeIn 1
programs.description: **135. AutoFadeIn 1** (Chorus+Rvb, 80 BPM). An automatic fade-in: the AR (Mono Lvl ≥ 31, attack 76 steps ≈ 1.5 s at first, release 39) raises the input level 124 → 160, widens the image (315 → 405) and opens the High Cut (47 → 111); the AR also lengthens its own attack as it rises (14 → 54 steps). Chorus voices (0 ms, deep) and tempo echoes (1/2 beat left, 3/2 beat right, ∓0.6 / +0.4 feedback). ADJUST = FX Mix.

programs.name: AutoFadeIn 2
programs.description: **136. AutoFadeIn 2** (Chorus+Rvb, 80 BPM). The fade-in with its attack on ADJUST ("Fade Rate": AR attack 0 … 150 steps, stored 45 ≈ 0.9 s): input level 136 → 160, High Cut 47 → 111, voices 3 / 6 (1/2-beat echoes) swapping sides. Chorus voices at 0–17 ms. Reverb 4.5 s at 0.71.

programs.name: AutoFadeIn 3
programs.description: **137. AutoFadeIn 3** (Chorus+Rvb, 70 BPM). The fade-in (attack 7 → 19 steps as it rises, release 4) on tempo echoes (2, 3, 4, 5 beats × 11 % and two 1/2-beat × 11 % voices, 47–142 ms) with a short reverb (0.5 s). ADJUST ("Rvb Lvl") sets Rvb Out 0 … 15.

programs.name: ChordSwells
programs.description: **138. ChordSwells** (Chorus+Rvb, 80 BPM). Swelling chords: slow chorus voices at 200 ms … 1.2 s with feedback (+0.25 / −0.2 / −0.4) build up sustained layers; the AR (attack 14 → 100 steps as it rises, release 74 steps) fades the input in (136 → 160), opens the High Cut and swaps voices 3 / 6. Reverb 4.5 s. ADJUST ("Rvb Lvl") = Rvb Out 0 … 15.

programs.name: BowedChords
programs.description: **139. BowedChords** (Chamber, 44 BPM; *Part I*). Bowed attacks: the AR (trigger Mono Lvl ≥ 5, attack 63 steps = 1.26 s, release 9) fades the input in from −40 dB to 0 dB at every new note, removing the attack. Delay voices: 0 ms left, 5 ms right and two 1/4-beat echoes (341 ms) with −0.46 feedback into a 2.3 s chamber. ADJUST = FX Mix (stored 92).

programs.name: BowedEchoes
programs.description: **140. BowedEchoes** (Chamber, 81 BPM). Bowed echoes: voices 2 / 4 at 1/2 beat (371 ms, left / right) whose feedback falls while playing and rises after (AR, Mono Lvl ≥ 5, attack 27, release 9 steps: feedback master 85 → 22, i.e. about −0.8 → −0.2), while the input level swells 130 → 160 with the same envelope; voices 1 / 3 at 0 ms. ADJUST = FX Mix (stored 65).

programs.name: Pedal Swell
programs.description: **141. Pedal Swell** (Chorus+Rvb, 120 BPM). A volume-pedal swell into chorus and echoes: the Footpedal sets the input level (80 = off → 160). Voices 1, 2, 5, 6 are 400-ms echoes (+0.2 feedback, chorused) and voices 3 / 4 a 0-ms chorus, all with 145-sample sweeps at 0.4 Hz; reverb 3.9 s at 0.16. ADJUST = FX Mix. Without a pedal the input passes at full level (16.1).

programs.name: RezClimber
programs.description: **142. RezClimber** (Res1>Plate, 81 BPM). A climbing arpeggio of resonances: each note above Mono Lvl 7 starts the AR (One Shot, attack 50 steps ≈ 1 s), which steps Assign through 0, 7, 12, 17 (plus the ADJUST offset "Tuning" 0 … 60, stored 19), and each new Assign value tunes the next resonator in turn (Res1 round robin, 14.4): root, fifth, octave, eleventh build up and ring. The input level sets the resonance (Mono Lvl → Mstr Res 0 … 100). Input voices at tempo fractions × 7 %, unison on. At rest no resonator is assigned (13.4).

programs.name: Chord Walk
programs.description: **143. Chord Walk** (Res2>Plate, 90 BPM). A walking chord: the Res2 harmoniser builds a six-note chord on Assign; Sw 1 (ramp, 8 beats) steps Assign through 36, 38, 40, 41 (C, D, E, F), Sw 2 (pulse, 8 beats) shifts the Root by 4, and the LFO bends voice 6's interval (44 → 48), so the chord changes in tempo; strong negative loop feedback (−0.975) makes each resonator ring an octave lower with odd harmonics (13.4). The input voices 1 and 4 are set by tempo-coded patches from Sw 1 / Sw 2 (16.6): 4 beats × Delay Master 50 % = 1 333 ms, 8/3 beat (888 ms) while the switch is at its top. ADJUST ("High Cut") = resonator high cut.

programs.name: Mars Bars
programs.description: **144. Mars Bars** (Res1>Plate, 81 BPM). Evolving clusters: the LFO (cosine, 6 beats per cycle) steps Assign through 36, 44, 59–66, and each new value is handed to the next resonator (round robin), so the six resonators collect a changing set of notes; resonators alternate positive (bright) and negative (hollow, octave-down) resonance. Input voices at 1, 1/2, 3/2 and 2/3 beat with feedback. ADJUST ("High Cut") = resonator high cut. Reverb 3.3 s at 0.89.

programs.name: ModalImpulse
programs.description: **145. ModalImpulse** (Res2>Plate, 80 BPM). An arpeggiated chord of near-infinite resonators (loop feedback ±0.999): E3, G3, B3, C3, C4, G3, excited one after the other by input voices at 0, 2/3, 1, 4/3, 5/3 and 2 beats, so an impulse rings out as a slowly building chord. ADJUST ("Tone") opens the resonator high cut (71 → 121) and lowers the resonance (100 → 57).

programs.name: MajorMinor
programs.description: **146. MajorMinor** (Res2>Plate, 81 BPM). A chord that grows and changes mode: the sawtooth LFO (24 beats per cycle) raises Active from 0 to 6 resonators, the pulse of the same LFO switches the scale between major and minor each half-cycle, and input voices at 3/2 … 7/2 beats feed them. Sw 1 (patched to Root) has trigger "none ≥ 1" and does not run on its own. ADJUST ("Tone") = resonator high cut and resonance. At rest Active is 0: no resonator rings, but the input voices still reach the output through the loop low-passes (14.4).

programs.name: MIDIchords
programs.description: **147. MIDIchords** (Res2>Plate, 120 BPM). Resonant chords played from MIDI: the highest held note (High Note) sets Assign, the harmoniser tunes six resonators to the chord (full resonance), note velocity sets their level, the sine LFO widens and narrows the image (135 ↔ 585), and the AR on the input moves FX Adjust. Until MIDI notes arrive the patches from High Note and Velocity have no value (16.1): the stored Assign 48 sets the chord (on C4) and ADJUST alone sets the level. ADJUST ("Sparkle", 0 … 5) opens the high cuts and raises the resonator level.

programs.name: LvlSweeper
programs.description: **148. LvlSweeper** (Res1>Plate, 120 BPM). Level-driven pitch: loud input (Mono Lvl ≥ 35) starts the AR, whose release (62 steps) walks Assign down through a stepped curve (60 … 24), assigning a falling series of notes to the resonators in turn as each note decays; the AR also sets the resonator level and resonance. Sw 1&2 (2 Hz pulses, triggered by the input) pan the output. Input voices at 1/3 … 1/8 beat. ADJUST ("Color") offsets Assign 0 … 24.

programs.name: Sweeper
programs.description: **149. Sweeper** (Res1>Plate, 120 BPM). A rising sweep of resonances: the sawtooth LFO (1 beat per cycle) sweeps Assign 36 → 60, so each beat the round robin hands a rising run of notes to the six resonators; Sw 1 (ramp, 4 beats) pans the output. Input voices at 1/2 … 3/5 beat, reverb with 2-beat echoes. ADJUST ("Pitch") offsets Assign 0 … 36. The AR (Foot Sw 1) drives nothing.

programs.name: MIDIsustain
programs.description: **150. MIDIsustain** (Res1>Plate, 120 BPM). A sustain-pedal resonator: the last MIDI note sets Assign (round robin); Foot Sw 2 (sustain) triggers the AR (attack 2, release 33), which raises Active 0 → 6, stops clearing the input lines and switches unison off, and the switch itself sets the resonance (98 → 100). Without a footswitch Active stays 0 and no resonator sounds. The LFO (2.1 Hz) moves the reverb echo times. ADJUST ("Bright") = Rt HC, Low Rt and resonator level.

programs.name: Small+Stage
programs.description: **151. Small+Stage** (Concert Hall, 120 BPM; *Part I*). A small hall (2.3 s, Size 136) with a stage: four early voices (9–37 ms × 70 %, diffused) around the image. ADJUST ("Stage Lvl", 0 … 50) raises the voices (Levels Master 20 → 50) and the voice share (FX Mix 100 → 66). The input levels pan voices 2 and 4 toward the centre as the left / right signal gets louder.

modulation.Modulated taps: Chorus 8 → D = 7: step every 2.86 samples, tap speed 66 smp/s

programs.name: Small Room
programs.description: **152. Small Room** (Chamber, 120 BPM; *Part I*). A small room (Size 27, 1.56 s at the knob), reverb only, with early reflections at 2 / 3 ms; ADJUST ("Liveness") sets Mid Rt and Shape together along a two-segment curve.

programs.name: Living Room
programs.description: **153. Living Room** (Chamber, 120 BPM; *Part I*). A short, soft room (Size 42, 0.63 s), reverb only; ADJUST ("Decay") = Mid Rt 0 … 60.

programs.name: Brick Kick
programs.description: **154. Brick Kick** (Chamber, 120 BPM; *Part I*). A tight, hard room for kick drum (0.40 s, Link off) with two early voices (17 ms left, 29 ms right) and reflections; ADJUST ("Liveness") brightens and reshapes the decay (Rt HC 10 → 34, Crossover, Shape 10 → 186).

programs.name: Large Room
programs.description: **155. Large Room** (Chamber, 120 BPM; *Part I*). A large room (Size 64, 1.89 s at the knob), reverb only; ADJUST ("Decay") = Mid Rt 0 … 59.

programs.name: SnareChamber
programs.description: **156. SnareChamber** (Chamber, 120 BPM; *Part I*). A short bright chamber for snare (0.42 s) with the Brick Kick early voices and reflections; ADJUST ("Liveness") as Brick Kick over 0 … 60.

programs.name: Tiled Room
programs.description: **157. Tiled Room** (Chamber, 120 BPM; *Part I*). A small tiled room (Size 23, 2.32 s) with two very early voices (2 ms left, 4 ms right); ADJUST ("Decay") = Mid Rt 0 … 62.

programs.name: Rich Chamber
programs.description: **158. Rich Chamber** (Chamber, 120 BPM; *Part I*). A dense, dark chamber (Diffusion 86, 2.45 s), reverb only; ADJUST ("Decay") = Mid Rt 0 … 61.

programs.name: Vox Chamber
programs.description: **159. Vox Chamber** (Chamber, 100 BPM; *Part I*). A long vocal chamber (6.8 s, Size 127) with four early voices (5–15 ms) and tank echoes at 354 / 350 ms whose feedback rises while singing (AR on Mono Lvl ≥ 46, attack 3, release 50 steps: EkoFbk 15 → 20). ADJUST ("Liveness") sets Rt HC and Shape (0 … 254).

programs.name: Locker Room
programs.description: **160. Locker Room** (Chamber, 120 BPM; *Part I*). A short hard room (Size 21, 2.45 s) with two early voices, reflections and a 14-ms post-delay mixed in (PstMix 100); ADJUST ("Depth") = Rt HC, Crossover and Shape.

programs.name: Wide Chamber
programs.description: **161. Wide Chamber** (Chamber, 94 BPM; *Part I*). A wide chamber (Rvb Width 413, AP Sweep 19, 1.64 s), reverb only; ADJUST ("Decay") = Mid Rt 0 … 60.

programs.name: Gate Chamber
programs.description: **162. Gate Chamber** (Inverse, 95 BPM; *Part I*). A gated reverb (Inverse algorithm, flat-ish Shape 16): ADJUST ("Duration", 0 … 64) sets the gate length (Duration 0 … 112, stored 56).

programs.name: Vox Plate
programs.description: **163. Vox Plate** (Plate, 97 BPM; *Part I*). A vocal plate (3.34 s at the knob, Attack 23) with two 3-ms voices and tempo-locked tank echoes (1 beat and 7/8 beat); ADJUST ("Decay", 0 … 30) = Mid Rt 30 … 60.

programs.name: Good olPlate
programs.description: **164. Good olPlate** (Plate, 100 BPM; *Part I*). A classic plate (3.86 s), reverb only, post-delay mix 100 with a small post-delay offset on the right; ADJUST = Mid Rt 0 … 60.

programs.name: Slap Plate
programs.description: **165. Slap Plate** (Plate, 106 BPM; *Part I*). A plate (2.93 s) with two slap-back voices (72 ms left, 40 ms right); ADJUST = Mid Rt 26 … 59.

programs.name: Brass Plate
programs.description: **166. Brass Plate** (Plate, 100 BPM; *Part I*). A bright, dense plate (Diffusion 93, 2.93 s) with two 5-ms voices; ADJUST = Mid Rt 30 … 61.

programs.name: Drum Plate
programs.description: **167. Drum Plate** (Plate, 100 BPM; *Part I*). A short drum plate (2.2 s, Attack 25) with voices at 23 / 7 ms and reflections; ADJUST = Mid Rt 34 … 59.

programs.name: Rich Plate
programs.description: **168. Rich Plate** (Plate, 100 BPM; *Part I*). A very dense plate (Diffusion 98, Attack 58, 3.86 s), reverb only; ADJUST = Mid Rt 0 … 62.

programs.name: Concert Wave
programs.description: **169. Concert Wave** (Concert Hall, 86 BPM; *Part I*). A large hall (Size 304) that "waves": the tempo-locked LFO (one cycle per 2 beats, 0.714 Hz; 16.3) moves both post-delays (0 → 21 / 23 → 0, PstMix 88) and, through its square output, the reverb width (360 ↔ 405); its triangle also selects the LFO shape. ADJUST ("Wave Knob", 0 … 40) sets Mid Rt (18 → 53), Diffusion (100 → 2) and Def (1 → 100).

modulation.Modulated taps: Chorus 10 → D = 1: step every 1.31 samples, tap speed 143 smp/s

programs.name: Concert Hall
programs.description: **170. Concert Hall** (Concert Hall, 120 BPM; *Part I*). A large concert hall (Size 271, 3.59 s) with early voices at 0 / 135 / 139 ms and post-delays of 139 ms; ADJUST ("Decay", 0 … 100) = Mid Rt 0 … 60. It decays faster than displayed (4.2).

modulation.Modulated taps: Chorus 10 → D = 1: step every 1.31 samples, tap speed 143 smp/s

programs.name: ConcertHall2
programs.description: **171. ConcertHall2** (Concert Hall, 120 BPM; *Part I*). A concert hall with reflections and 147-ms post-delays; ADJUST ("Empty/Full", 0 … 15) shortens and darkens it as the hall "fills" (Mid Rt 50 → 35, Rt HC 29 → 16).

modulation.Modulated taps: Chorus 8 → D = 7: step every 2.86 samples, tap speed 66 smp/s

programs.name: Piano Hall
programs.description: **172. Piano Hall** (Concert Hall, 120 BPM; *Part I*). A hall for piano (3.59 s) with four early voices (0 / 31 / 0 / 26 ms, slight feedback, diffused 67). The AR (Mono Lvl ≥ 31, attack 36, release 67 steps) opens the post-delays (0 → 26 / 27) while playing, and Sw 1 (ramp, 3.85-s cycle, triggered at Mono Lvl ≥ 75) narrows the reverb on loud passages. ADJUST = Mid Rt 0 … 61.

modulation.Modulated taps: Chorus 9 → D = 4: step every 2.09 samples, tap speed 90 smp/s

programs.name: Medium Hall
programs.description: **173. Medium Hall** (Concert Hall, 120 BPM; *Part I*). A medium hall (Size 192, 2.32 s), reverb only; ADJUST = Mid Rt 0 … 60.

modulation.Modulated taps: Chorus 8 → D = 7: step every 2.86 samples, tap speed 66 smp/s

programs.name: Vocal Hall
programs.description: **174. Vocal Hall** (Concert Hall, 120 BPM; *Part I*). A vocal hall (4.54 s at the knob) with tempo-locked reflections (1/6 beat) and post-delays (1/2 and 3/7 beat); ADJUST = Mid Rt 0 … 58.

modulation.Modulated taps: Chorus 9 → D = 4: step every 2.09 samples, tap speed 90 smp/s

programs.name: Deep Space
programs.description: **175. Deep Space** (Chorus+Rvb, 120 BPM; *Part I*). A huge, dark ambience (12.7 s, pre-delay 137) behind a chorus (voices 7–43 ms) and two half-second echoes (+0.3 feedback); the AR (Mono Lvl ≥ 37, attack 10, release 83 steps) brightens the reverb while playing (Rt HC 11 → 27) and speeds the width LFO (0.02 → 0.47 Hz, triangle on FX Width 388 ↔ 410). ADJUST = FX Mix (stored 69).

programs.name: Plate4 Horns
programs.description: **176. Plate4 Horns** (Plate, 120 BPM; *Part I*). A horn plate with two early voices (28 / 22 ms) and reflections; ADJUST ("Impact", 0 … 100) raises the decay (Mid Rt 0 → 59) and the attack (0 → 100) together.

programs.name: Alley Slap
programs.description: **177. Alley Slap** (Plate, 120 BPM; *Part I*). A slap-back alley: a very short plate (Mid Rt 0) with tempo-locked tank echoes (1/8 and 1/9 beat) and feedback; ADJUST sets the pre-delay (6 … 100).

programs.name: Drum Gate
programs.description: **178. Drum Gate** (Inverse, 120 BPM; *Part I*). A gated drum reverb (Shape 255) whose width follows the left input envelope (Env L → Rvb Width 416 → 361 while loud); ADJUST ("Duration", 0 … 70) sets both the gate length (Duration 22 … 112) and the envelope release (17 … 35).

programs.name: Slope Down
programs.description: **179. Slope Down** (Inverse, 120 BPM; *Part I*). An inverse reverb (Duration 94) whose post-delays are swept by the AR in Repeat mode while the input is loud (Mono Lvl ≥ 64, attack 75 steps): PstDly 10 → 682 with PstMix 0 → 70, a long sliding echo. ADJUST = Duration 0 … 112.

programs.name: BigBoomRoom
programs.description: **180. BigBoomRoom** (Chamber, 120 BPM; *Part I*). A boomy room (1.31 s) whose post-delays open with the input envelopes (Env L → PstDly R, Env R → PstDly L); the input level is also patched to the LFO rate, but nothing is patched from the LFO; ADJUST ("BoomKnob", 0 … 36) raises the low-frequency decay (Low Rt 4 → 9) and crossover (8 → 20).

programs.name: Whammy Hall
programs.description: **181. Whammy Hall** (Concert Hall, 120 BPM; *Part I*). A hall (4.54 s at the knob) with a fast vibrato on the post-delays (LFO cosine, 4.98 Hz) that loud playing switches off: the AR (Mono Lvl ≥ 73, release 114 steps) takes the LFO depth to 0 and lets it return over 2.3 s. ADJUST = Mid Rt 30 … 60.

modulation.Modulated taps: Chorus 10 → D = 1: step every 1.31 samples, tap speed 143 smp/s

programs.name: JetChamber
programs.description: **182. JetChamber** (Chamber, 120 BPM; *Part I*). A jet-flanged chamber (7.7 s): the sine LFO (0.08 Hz) moves the two post-delays in opposite directions (23 ↔ 0); ADJUST ("Jet Knob") sets PstMix 0 … 50, i.e. the flange depth. AP Sweep 31, tank echoes at 23 / 23.

programs.name: EnvChamber
programs.description: **183. EnvChamber** (Chamber, 120 BPM; *Part I*). JetChamber with the post-delays moved by the AR (Mono Lvl ≥ 28, attack 20, release 13 steps) instead of the LFO: the flange sweeps with each phrase.

programs.name: Wizz & Wazz
programs.description: **184. Wizz & Wazz** (Plate, 81 BPM). Everything on one tempo LFO (4 beats per cycle): voice 1 (12 ↔ 23 ms, sine) and voice 3 (34 ↔ 12 ms, triangle) sweep and flange, the post-delays rise and fall, and the sawtooth pans the whole output from left to right and crossfades voices → reverb (FX Mix 0 → 100) each cycle; voices 2 / 4 are long tempo echoes (17/18 and 9/10 beat) with +0.3 feedback, all diffused (Voice Dif 100). ADJUST ("Decay") = Mid Rt 0 … 60.

programs.name: Sci Fi
programs.description: **185. Sci Fi** (Chamber, 120 BPM). A tiny, short chamber (Size 0, 0.6 s, reverb only) with a vibrato on the post-delays (triangle LFO, opposite directions, 0 ↔ 57) whose rate falls while playing (AR: 3.2 → 1.26 Hz). ADJUST ("Wiggle") = LFO depth.

programs.name: Wobble Plate
programs.description: **186. Wobble Plate** (Plate, 120 BPM). A 4.5 s plate (reverb only) with its post-delays moved by triangle and cosine (0.26 Hz); ADJUST ("Wobble") sets the delay glide response (GldResp 30 … 60), i.e. how strongly the moving delays bend the pitch.

programs.name: Dyna Vibrato
programs.description: **187. Dyna Vibrato** (Glide>Hall, 117 BPM). A dynamic vibrato on gliding taps: the triangle LFO moves the four glide taps (up to 12–15 ms), but its rate and depth follow the input level (quiet: 5.3 Hz at depth 38; loud: 2.0 Hz at depth 0), so the vibrato appears as notes decay. ADJUST ("Glide") sets the B taps' base delay (0 … 42 ms). Glide feedback +0.19 / −0.12, diffused echo voices at 0 ms, short hall (0.76 s).

programs.name: VibroVerb
programs.description: **188. VibroVerb** (Chamber, 120 BPM). A 1.4 s chamber (reverb only) with a vibrato on the post-delays (triangle, 0 ↔ 57); the AR in Repeat mode (while Mono Lvl ≥ 24) cycles the LFO rate between 4.1 and 1.6 Hz. ADJUST ("V-Depth") = LFO depth.

programs.name: SweepVerb
programs.description: **189. SweepVerb** (Chamber, 120 BPM). A 3.1 s chamber (reverb only) whose post-delays sweep apart on each attack (AR, Mono Lvl ≥ 32, attack 13, release 20 steps: PstDly L 0 → 114, R 114 → 0); ADJUST sets the glide response (GldResp 0 … 100), i.e. how fast and how pitched the sweep is.

programs.name: EnveloVerb
programs.description: **190. EnveloVerb** (Chamber, 120 BPM). A ducking, blooming reverb: at rest a 21 s chamber; while the input is loud (AR, Mono Lvl ≥ 64, attack 1, release 75 steps) the decay drops (Mid Rt 61 → 51) and the reverb is pulled down (FX Mix 100 → 38), and after the input stops it returns over 1.5 s. ADJUST ("Rt HC") = 5 … 45.

programs.name: Super Ball!
programs.description: **191. Super Ball!** (Glide>Hall, 111 BPM). A bouncing ball: turning ADJUST to 1 triggers the AR in One Shot mode (attack 390 steps ≈ 7.8 s): the input to the echoes is cut (Gld Lvl → 0), the echo voices (1/2 beat left, right voice) get strong negative feedback (−1 → −0.9), and the Delay Master falls from 200 % to 4 %, so the captured sound bounces faster and faster; at the top the lines are cleared. Back to 0 resets it. A Latch on Foot Sw 1 is defined but not used.

programs.name: LevlStutter
programs.description: **192. LevlStutter** (M-Band+Rvb, 53 BPM). A six-tap stutter: the AR patches (tempo-coded, 16.6) replace the tempo values, so at rest tap j sits at j beats (1 132, 2 265, … 6 796 ms at 53 BPM; with the standard memory the taps beyond 2 730 ms are halved, 14.1), panned left to right; a loud input (Mono Lvl ≥ 40) starts the AR (One Shot, attack 5, release 50 steps), which divides every tap time by a denominator rising from 1 to 24 (down to j/24 beat, 47 ms steps) and back. The cosine LFO (16 beats) pans the output slowly. ADJUST = feedback master (stored 0). No reverb.

programs.name: Freez 2 of 8
programs.description: **193. Freez 2 of 8** (Glide>Hall, 81 BPM). A freeze looper with 1/2-beat loops (371 ms, left / right). Feedback on the loops is set by ADJUST (V1 / V4 Fbk 100 → 200, i.e. none → maximum, 0.99994 per pass: practically lossless, 14.3). Foot Sw 2 clears the loops. Sw 1 (pulse, 8 beats, width 12) is patched to freeze for part of every 8 beats (input cut via Gld Lvl, feedback to maximum), but its trigger is "none ≥ 1", which does not run on its own (6.3); a Latch on Foot Sw 1 is defined but not used.

programs.name: Freez 2over3
programs.description: **194. Freez 2over3** (Glide>Hall, 81 BPM). As Freez 2 of 8 with the right loop set by a tempo-coded Sw 1 patch (16.6): 1/2 beat, 1/3 beat while Sw 1 is at its top (two against three), feedback set by ADJUST (left 100 → 200, right 100 → 178).

programs.name: Freeze&Speed
programs.description: **195. Freeze&Speed** (Glide>Hall, 125 BPM). ADJUST is the freeze switch (0 / 1, through the AR: attack 0, release 56 steps): at 1 the 1/4-beat loops (left / right) take the maximum feedback, the input is cut from them, the dry-through voices 2 / 5 go off, the reverb input opens (Rvb In 0 → 80) and the Delay Master steps 80 → 125 %; back at 0 the release moves the Delay Master through 100 → 80 % (the loop repeats speed up) before normal operation resumes. Sw 1 (Foot Sw 1) drives nothing.

programs.name: ADJToFreeze
programs.description: **196. ADJToFreeze** (Glide>Hall, 81 BPM). ADJUST as a direct freeze switch: 0 = the input passes (voices 2 / 5 at 0 ms, reverb input closed); 1 = 1-beat loops (voices 1 / 4) at maximum feedback with the input cut and the reverb fed by the loops.

programs.name: ADJToFreeze2
programs.description: **197. ADJToFreeze2** (Glide>Hall, 81 BPM). ADJToFreeze with loops of 1/3 beat (left) and 1/2 beat (right), a cross-rhythm when frozen, and the reverb out of the mix.

programs.name: FSw2 Freeze
programs.description: **198. FSw2 Freeze** (Glide>Hall, 81 BPM). A footswitch freeze: Foot Sw 2 through a Latch (low 0 / high 100) gives push-on / push-off; on, the 1/2-beat loops go to maximum feedback and the input is cut from them. Foot Sw 1 clears. ADJUST sets the loop feedback when not frozen (100 → 200, stored 131).

programs.name: FSw2 Speedup
programs.description: **199. FSw2 Speedup** (Glide>Hall, 79 BPM). Freeze&Speed on Foot Sw 2: the AR (attack 0) freezes the 1/4-beat loops at once with the Delay Master at 200 %, and on release (length set by ADJUST "How Long?": AR release 0 … 500 steps, stored 155) the Delay Master runs down 200 → 100 → 16 %, so the frozen loop repeats faster and faster before normal operation resumes.

programs.name: LongestLoop
programs.description: **200. LongestLoop** (Glide>Hall, 120 BPM). The longest loop: the input (both channels panned left) is written into 2.5-s echo lines; voice 1 feeds the left line into the right line at maximum cross feedback. At rest Mix is 0 (dry only) while the lines keep recording. Foot Sw 2 through a Latch (push-on / push-off) closes the loop: voice 4's cross feedback goes to maximum, so the two 2.5-s lines form one 5-s loop, the input to the loop is cut, voice 4 is heard and Mix goes to 100 (wet). Foot Sw 1 clears. ADJUST = FX Mix (stored 0: no reverb). With the standard delay memory the 2.5-s lines also fit (11.1).
